title: MATH 21 Mastery Challenge: Matrices & Linear Systems
description: Comprehensive 22-question 4-quadrant companion mastery exam for MATH 21. Rigorously tests matrix multiplication, determinant properties, inverses, eigenvalues/trace relations, Cramer's rule, and matrix calculator mode bypasses under timed board conditions.

questions.promptText: If $A$ is an $n \times n$ square matrix and $k$ is a scalar constant, what is the value of **$\det(k A)$**?
questions.explanation: Factoring the scalar $k$ out of each of the $n$ rows of matrix $A$ multiplies the determinant by $k$ a total of $n$ times: $\det(kA) = k^n\det A$.

questions.promptText: What is the relationship between the **Trace of a matrix ($\text{Tr}(A)$)** and its **Eigenvalues ($\lambda_i$)**?
questions.choiceA: The Trace equals the sum of all eigenvalues: Tr(A) = ∑ λᵢ.
questions.choiceB: The Trace equals the product of all eigenvalues.
questions.choiceC: The Trace equals the maximum eigenvalue.
questions.choiceD: The Trace equals the square root of the determinant.
questions.explanation: In linear algebra, the sum of the main diagonal entries $\text{Tr}(A) = \sum a_{ii}$ strictly equals the sum of all eigenvalues $\sum \lambda_i$.

questions.promptText: A square matrix $A$ is defined as **Singular** if and only if:
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular if its determinant is zero, meaning its rows are linearly dependent and it cannot be inverted ($A^{-1}$ does not exist).

questions.promptText: Which property strictly defines a real **Orthogonal Matrix**?
questions.choiceA: Aᵀ = A⁻¹ (its transpose is equal to its inverse).
questions.explanation: An orthogonal matrix satisfies $A A^T = I$, which is algebraically equivalent to $A^T = A^{-1}$.

questions.promptText: If matrix $A$ has dimension $3 \times 4$ and matrix $B$ has dimension $4 \times 2$, what is the dimension of their product matrix **$C = AB$**?
questions.explanation: Multiplication of $A_{m \times p} \times B_{p \times n}$ produces product matrix $C_{m \times n}$. Here $(3 \times 4) \times (4 \times 2) = (3 \times 2)$.

questions.promptText: What is the **product of all eigenvalues** of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$?
questions.explanation: Setting $\lambda = 0$ in the characteristic polynomial $\det(A - \lambda I) = 0$ proves that the product of all eigenvalues equals $\det A$.

questions.promptText: Evaluate the determinant of the 2x2 matrix: $\begin{pmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$.
Find the determinant of the 3x3 matrix: $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$.
If $A$ and $B$ are square matrices of identical size with $\det(A) = 3$ and $\det(B) = -4$, what is **$\det(AB)$**?
questions.explanation: By the multiplicative property of determinants: $\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B) = (3)(-4) = -12$.

questions.promptText: Find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$.
Find the **Trace** of the 3x3 matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 6 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$.
Find the inverse of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$.
If $A$ is a 3x3 matrix with $\det(A) = 4$, find the value of **$\det(3 A)$**.

In circuit analysis, three mesh loop currents satisfy the matrix system $\begin{pmatrix} 4 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 6 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} I_1 \\ I_2 \\ I_3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Find the determinant of the impedance matrix.
An RF two-port network has scattering parameter matrix $S = \begin{pmatrix} 0.2 & 0.8 \\ 0.8 & 0.2 \end{pmatrix}$. Find the determinant of the S-parameter matrix.

A 2D stress element in Mohr's circle analysis has plane stress tensor $\sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 80 & 30 \\ 30 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\text{ MPa}$. Find the maximum principal stress (the maximum eigenvalue $\lambda_1$).
What is the **Rank** of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$?
questions.explanation: Row 2 ($2, 4, 6$) is linearly dependent on Row 1 ($2 \times R_1$). Rows 1 and 3 are linearly independent, so the maximum number of independent rows is 2.

questions.promptText: Using Cramer's Rule, solve for $x$ in the linear system: $2x + 3y = 8$ and $4x - y = 2$.
What is the common trap when computing the determinant of a scaled matrix $\det(k A)$ for a 3x3 matrix?
questions.choiceA: Writing $k \det A$ instead of $k^3 \det A$, forgetting to raise the scalar $k$ to the power of the matrix dimension $n = 3$.
questions.explanation: Multiplying a matrix by scalar $k$ multiplies every single row by $k$. For an $n \times n$ matrix, this scales the determinant by $k^n$.

questions.promptText: When inverting a 2x2 matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$, what is the correct adjugate matrix formula?
questions.explanation: For a 2x2 matrix, swap the main diagonal elements ($a \leftrightarrow d$) and negate the off-diagonal elements ($-b, -c$): $\text{adj}(A) = \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.promptText: Using the 3-second Trace-Determinant shortcut, what are the eigenvalues of $\begin{pmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$?
If $\det(A) = 8$, what is $\det(A^{-1})$ in 1 second?
